frequency_question: How often has an incremental reserve ratio tool been activated by central banks in this reference class within a similar time horizon?
membership_rule: Members are central banks of major emerging market economies (such as India, Brazil, Indonesia, or South Africa) utilizing liquidity management tools categorized specifically as incremental or marginal reserve ratio requirements on banking liabilities during periods of excess liquidity management. Excluded are standard, non-incremental changes to baseline reserve requirements or open market operations.
window: A four-month operational window corresponding to the resolution timeframe.

cases.name: Bank Indonesia secondary reserve requirement adjustment 2021
Central Bank of Brazil compulsory deposit requirement tweak 2022
Bank of Korea liquidity adjustment ratio 2011
Bank Indonesia primary reserve requirement increase 2018
Central Bank of Turkey reserve option mechanism adjustment 2017

coverage_note: 8 named reference instances; believed to represent a comprehensive sample of major emerging market deployments of this specific variant over recent decades.
known_gaps: Excludes minor interventions by smaller emerging market jurisdictions with non-comparable data transparency.
skeleton: Emerging market central bank liquidity management cycles over the past 25 years, parsed by frequency of deploying targeted marginal/incremental reserve requirements during liquidity overhang periods.
multiplier: 8 observed instances across comparable systemic liquidity management cycles, yielding 3 hits for the specific incremental reserve ratio tool within the defined window parameters.
validity_reason: Central banking liquidity frameworks and the structural usage of marginal reserve tools evolve slowly across multi-year monetary policy regimes.
